title: Crystal-graph learning and DFT identify 19,512 additional thermodynamically stable materials
summary: The authors trained crystal-graph attention networks on an expanded, composition- and symmetry-balanced dataset and used them to search 2,500 binary and ternary structure prototypes covering about one billion inorganic compounds. Density-functional-theory validation identified 19,512 additional compounds on the calculated thermodynamic convex hull and about 150,000 more within 50 meV/atom of it; the paper also analyzed predicted superconducting and superhard materials and compounds with large gap deformation potentials.
ai_technology: Crystal-graph attention neural networks trained on expanded density-functional-theory materials data
organization: Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg; University of Coimbra; Friedrich Schiller University Jena

evidence.tested: The authors trained crystal-graph attention networks on an expanded, composition- and symmetry-balanced dataset and used them to search 2,500 binary and ternary structure prototypes covering about one billion inorganic compounds.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint and the reported stable compounds are computationally predicted, with DFT convex-hull validation; the study does not report their experimental synthesis. Stability depends on the calculated structures and thermodynamic reference data. The additional ~150,000 compounds are near-hull candidates, not counted as thermodynamically stable discoveries in the title or summary.
evidence.ai_role: The graph networks accelerated screening of roughly one billion prototype-generated candidates, after which density-functional-theory calculations validated stability for identified candidates; machine learning plus ab initio calculations also ranked materials for selected functional properties.
